title: Fixed daily models gave a rain slope loss in annual runoff departures at 29 south-east Australian gauges in 1997-2009
abstract: We test whether a lower rain slope of annual runoff departures must show a change in catchment properties. We reuse published annual results from fixed daily GR4J and SIMHYD models. On a common set of 29 south-east Australian gauges, the observed 1997-2009 departure slope was -0.853, and the mean fixed-model slope was -0.640. Units are percentage of reference mean runoff per percentage of reference mean rain. The remaining slope was -0.213, with conditional 95 percent year-block and spatial-cell limits of -0.468 to +0.061. In 2010-2021 the remaining slope was -0.277 (-0.547 to -0.059), but the remaining slope difference between eras was unclear: -0.064 (-0.418 to +0.274). Removing reference quadratic curvature gave a negative remaining slope in both eras. Restricting rain to reference support made both intervals include zero. Rain product and PET treatment also changed the limits. Thus fixed daily models can give a large rain slope loss with no parameter change. The annual slope alone does not identify a new catchment state. This is an exploratory analysis of stored model results. It is not independent data confirmation or a physical cause test. Reference fits, model fits and measurement error are not resampled.
